## Description
&#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;The chemical formula for Mylar (biaxially-oriented polyethylene terephthalate or BoPET) is:&#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;(C₁₀H₈O₄)ₙ&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;C₁₀H₈O₄ represents the repeating monomer unit derived from the reaction of &#10;&#9;&#9;terephthalic acid and ethylene glycol. &#10;&#9;&#9;n indicates the number of repeating units in the polymer chain, which varies depending &#10;&#9;&#9;on the molecular weight of the specific resin used.&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;In this process, the carboxyl groups (–COOH) of the acid react with the hydroxyl groups (–OH)&#10;&#9;&#9;of the glycol to form ester linkages, releasing water as a byproduct. &#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;General Equation: nC8H6O4 + nC2H6O2  → [-C10H8O4-]n + 2nH2O&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;In industrial settings, this is often a two-step process involving an intermediate &#10;&#9;&#9;called bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate or BHET, but the net stoichiometry remains the same:&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;1 mole of acid reacts with 1 mole of glycol to form 1 mole of repeating unit and 2 moles of water.)&#10;&#9;&#9;
